newsitem.title: JAPAN: AT&T says call-back service meets govt rules.
newsitem.headline: AT&T says call-back service meets govt rules.

text.p: AT & T Communications Services Japan said on Wednesday that the international cut-rate call-back service it launched in Tokyo today is consistent with government guidelines in both countries.

"We have completely discussed with the Japanese and the Federal Communications Commission of the U.S. ... Our service is consistent with the current government guidelines," president and CEO at AT&T Corp Asia/Pacific, John Legere, told a news conference.

AT&T had previously opposed call-back service, calling it a mis-use of service. But it changed its stance since the international body, the International Telecommunications Union, declared in June 1995 that some kinds of call-back service are legal, he said. "The FCC now says it is actually good for competition," Legere said.
AT&T Communications announced that it started its first call-back service for corporate customers in Tokyo at rates of about half of Japanese international operators.

Corporate customers with monthly bills of more than 20,000 yen will be provided an "autodialer," which will direct the customers' calls through the AT & T Worldwide Intelligent Network, and connect the calls at cost-effective U.S. rates.
